correspondence.component_scope: Eastern headward hook in the Huancaccocha sector, then west to the upper Iruro valley
correspondence.finding: The selected line runs northward and then westward from an eastern headward arm. MTC Lucanas shows Laguna Huancaccocha separately from the Iruro river and omits a continuous hydrographic route over this selected hook. IGP Figure 42 depicts the upper basin, lake label and a dense drainage network, but its small raster does not resolve the particular selected headward branch and lake/river connector with sufficient clarity. The IGP prose's general lake-origin statement is not a substitute for that map correspondence.
correspondence.material_gap: Selected headward arm and westward connector into Iruro; not merely an unnamed reach, exact bank, vertex or mouth-point issue.

correspondence.component_scope: Iruro valley southward through the Lucanas uplands to the Pallpo/Santiago de Vado setting
correspondence.finding: The MTC Lucanas original shows the south-running Iruro through the Iruro–Pampahuasi–Telarhuasi–Orcohuasi corridor, continuing past Villa Achapara and toward Lucanas/Santiago de Vado. The selected southward valley and successive bends correspond at ordinary generalized corridor scale. The western tributary entering near Santiago de Vado is mapped; IGP prose identifies Pallpo as the tributary after which the main river is called San José. MTC uses its own upstream Acarí labelling, so exact legal name boundaries are not inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Lucanas and San Juan de Utec to the eastern Chilques tributary junction
correspondence.finding: The Lucanas map depicts the valley through the PE-30A crossing and southeastward past Lucanas and San Juan de Utec. Its southern coverage overlaps the San Pedro map, which shows the receiving trunk and the eastern tributary corridor from the Chilques/San Pedro area. The latter joins the selected trunk before its southward continuation. IGP prose calls this the Chilques confluence and describes the downstream river as Acarí. San José is a bounded prose name for the intervening reach, not a separately verified uniform label over every selected segment.

correspondence.component_scope: Central Acarí canyon and valley through the San Pedro–Saisa boundary corridor to the Arequipa boundary
correspondence.finding: The MTC San Pedro original continuously maps the trunk south and southwest past Upaca, Racrapampa, Puca Corral and the Piedra Cruz sector, then through the major westward bend near Marcona Baja–Palja and onward past Usahuacho and Huarato toward the Arequipa boundary. Repeated Acarí labels and ordinary river/boundary context support the selected middle corridor without requiring precise coincident vertices.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Acarí valley, Chaviña and Pacific outlet
correspondence.finding: The overlapping Acarí district original follows the named river southward through the cultivated valley and Acarí, then past Monasi and Monte Redondo to the PE-1S crossing at Puente Chaviña. Below that crossing it passes Americas Unidas and Musia and reaches the mapped Pacific coastline. This supports the actual receiving sea and mouth corridor, rather than only a model sea-terminal flag. No exact contemporary outlet position or bank alignment is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern headward opening and southwest transfer
correspondence.finding: The original depicts small lakes and streams in the selected northern headward terrain, with the Agnew River corridor nearby. It does not establish the selected complete southwestward transfer across this drainage area into Lord Lindsay River. A nearby Agnew label is not assigned to the selected feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Western junction, southward Lord Lindsay valley and eastward bend
correspondence.finding: The selected western and middle course corresponds at corridor scale to the south-running Lord Lindsay valley, its appreciable western tributary junction, and its turn east. The original depicts narrower river reaches, lateral feeders, alluvial areas and rapids; unnamed tributaries retain null names.

correspondence.component_scope: Sanagak junction and lower Lord Lindsay alluvial/lake passage
correspondence.finding: The mapped river meets the southern Sanagak Lake connection and continues south through an alluvial, locally divided channel and lake-rich lowland before bending northeast. Map-margin fish commentary independently relates the Lord Lindsay system to Thom Bay and mentions possible use of Sanagak Lake. This supports the mapped system context, not every possible lowland cross-channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Tukingayuk approach and selected southern transfer to Krusenstern Lake
correspondence.finding: The originals distinguish the northeastward Lord Lindsay Lake route from the southern Tukingayuk Lake area and the separate Krusenstern lake body. The selected southern/eastward connection between those lake areas cannot be established continuously from their depicted channels. The sheets cover this terrain, but coverage alone is not correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Krusenstern Lake passage
correspondence.finding: The selected final east/northeast lake passage corresponds to the northern arms of the mapped Krusenstern Lake. The two adjacent sheets show its continuation across their common boundary and distinguish it from Tukingayuk and Lord Lindsay lakes. The unsupported western entrance is retained separately.

correspondence.component_scope: Krusenstern outlet, Kogaluktok Falls and actual marine terminal
correspondence.finding: The original shows the lake narrowing into its northern outlet, the labeled Kogaluktok Falls, and discharge into the southwest part of Thom Bay, within the Gulf of Boothia. Lord Lindsay Lake has a separate bayward outlet farther north. No river hydronym for this Krusenstern outlet or exact contemporary tidal boundary is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected eastern opening and Park Canyon drainage
correspondence.finding: The selected eastern opening lies on the westward intermittent drainage beside Lockwood Valley Road, northwest of San Guillermo Mountain. The San Guillermo Mountain 2015 original depicts the drainage turning southwest into Park Canyon, then west through its lower canyon. The selected generalized course follows that same connected canyon system. Park Canyon is a canyon label; no independent stream hydronym is assigned to this opening.
correspondence.reading_scope: Original northern-sheet pixels and detailed private crops; composite terrain view used only for orientation where its small-channel hydrography is absent.

correspondence.component_scope: Park Canyon outlet, Wagon Road Canyon and Alamo Creek connection
correspondence.finding: The western edge of San Guillermo Mountain and adjoining eastern Reyes Peak sheet show the Park Canyon intermittent channel continuing into the Wagon Road Canyon setting and joining the Alamo Creek approach. The Reyes Peak original carries the connected wash westward into Dry Canyon. Nearby Beartrap Creek approaches from the south; the selected route stays on the east-to-west approach. The maps resolve the connector at ordinary corridor scale without fixing a confluence vertex.
correspondence.name_scope: The mapped receiving headwater stream only, not the entire selected opening or the distinct Alamo Creek near Twitchell Reservoir.
correspondence.reading_scope: Original map pixels on adjacent 2015 sheets, with the composite headward panel corroborating the broad corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Dry Canyon to Ozena-area bend and upper Cuyama valley
correspondence.finding: Reyes Peak 2015 labels the connected broad channel Cuyama River west of the Dry Canyon/Alamo approach. It continues past the Reyes Creek junction and the Ozena Camp Ground Road area, bends northwest near State Route 33, and enters the long upper valley. The composite upper panel continues the same river past side-canyon mouths, the Tinta Creek approach and Apache Canyon area toward Ventucopa. The eastern Alamo Creek and unnamed Park Canyon reach are not renamed Cuyama River.
correspondence.reading_scope: Original Reyes Peak northern corridor plus overlapping composite headward and upper-valley views.

correspondence.component_scope: Ventucopa and Ballinger Canyon through the central Cuyama Valley
correspondence.finding: The selected northwest course follows the broad, repeatedly labeled Cuyama River bed past Ventucopa and the Ballinger Canyon approach into the agricultural Cuyama Valley. The middle view traces the continuous river corridor north of State Route 166 and New Cuyama Airport, between the Caliente Range to the north and Sierra Madre Mountains to the south. New River and The Wash are separately mapped in the northern/eastern valley setting; their labels are not transferred to the selected Cuyama reach. No lake connector is required through this interval.
correspondence.reading_scope: Overlapping upper-valley and middle-valley original composite rasters.

correspondence.component_scope: Western valley and lower Cuyama canyon
correspondence.finding: The river continues northwest beneath the Caliente/Chalk Mountain setting, enters the western canyon corridor, turns around the northern bend and then southwest along the State Route 166 corridor. The mapped Cuyama River remains continuous through the canyon and past side-creek junctions toward the eastern arm of Twitchell Reservoir. The valley, canyon bend and reservoir entrance correspond to the selected course, rather than to an adjacent branch.
correspondence.reading_scope: Overlapping middle-valley and canyon/reservoir composite rasters.

correspondence.component_scope: Twitchell Reservoir, tributary arms and dam outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected Cuyama approach enters the reservoir from the east, continues through the impounded corridor, and leaves through the southern dam setting. The mapped Alamo Creek enters from the north/northeast and Huasna River from the northwest; these are separate tributary approaches rather than the selected upstream route. The USACE project page independently identifies both dam and reservoir as on the Cuyama River. Reservoir passage is described as a waterbody component, not assigned a uniform river name.
correspondence.reading_scope: Original canyon/reservoir and lower composite pixels; bounded USACE Background prose.

correspondence.component_scope: Cuyama River below Twitchell and Sisquoc junction
correspondence.finding: Below Twitchell Dam the selected channel runs south through the confined lower Cuyama valley and meets the separately mapped Sisquoc River approaching from the southeast. It then turns northwest into the channel labeled Santa Maria River. The USACE page and California Water Board overview independently describe the Cuyama and Sisquoc forming the Santa Maria River. The selected object follows the Cuyama approach, not the Sisquoc branch.
correspondence.reading_scope: Original canyon/reservoir and lower-river views, supported by the two directly opened primary prose pages.

correspondence.component_scope: Santa Maria valley and Guadalupe reach
correspondence.finding: From the confluence the selected course follows the mapped Santa Maria River northwest and west along the northern side of Santa Maria, past the Suey Creek approach and Highway 101/Nipomo Creek setting, then across the valley to Guadalupe and the Highway 1 crossing. The labeled river and broad bed remain continuous through the selected lower interval. Other nearby drainage, including the separate Oso Flaco coastal system, is not substituted for the selected terminal.
correspondence.reading_scope: Original lower-river/terminal raster; Water Board overview supports the westward confluence-to-ocean relation.

correspondence.component_scope: Coastal wetland/estuarine passage and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: West of Guadalupe the selected river corridor bends through the coastal floodplain and wetland/estuarine waterbody immediately behind the coastal dunes, reaching the Pacific shoreline in the Santa Maria River mouth setting. The mapped terminal is separate from Oso Flaco Creek farther north. The Water Board overview expressly places the Santa Maria River outlet at the Pacific Ocean. This is ordinary mouth-setting correspondence; present sand-bar opening, exact tidal channels, shoreline position and a precise mouth vertex are not established.
correspondence.reading_scope: Original lower-river/terminal composite pixels, with bounded primary prose for the receiving ocean.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern headward opening and initial lake/stream route
correspondence.finding: The eastern opening lies in the northwestern Lac Vernon sheet sector. The retained simplified geological figure does not show its small waterways, the survey-index map misses the extreme eastern start, and regional CEHQ hydrography does not distinguish the selected initial feeder and lake entrances/outlets. Actual headwater setting and all opening connections remain unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward upper/middle lake-rich corridor south of59°N
correspondence.finding: Primary CEHQ cartography places repeated Mariet labels on the westward drainage north of the separate Qilalugalik/Le Roy and Koktac settings. It includes a separate Lac Illuvigartalik label. The survey-index figure depicts the regional channel/lake arrangement through northern34K. These originals support the broad Mariet corridor, but their generalization and label/grid overlap do not establish every selected lake passage and material connector; no unverified lake identity is assigned to a particular selected passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestward middle continuation across59°N
correspondence.finding: The two independent originals show a west/northwest-running connected regional river/lake corridor in southern34N corresponding in general setting to the selected continuation. CEHQ carries the Mariet name, whereas the DP2017 figure supplies sheet-grid orientation. Small lateral-lake connections and selected major junction choices are not all resolved at the inspected scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Western lower widenings and tributary/branch junctions
correspondence.finding: Regional cartography depicts the western drainage and elongated waterbody/stream forms, but the north arrow on CEHQ and sheet labels/grid on the DP2017 index obscure parts of the lower path. The selected lower connections and material tributary/branch junctions are not fully distinguished. Discovery-only Saputiapiit and other names are not used to fill these gaps.

correspondence.component_scope: Final river outlet and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The DP2017 index supplies broad Hudson Bay coastal context south of59°15′N; CEHQ supports the Mariet regional drainage. Neither inspected original establishes the selected final outlet/channel and its continuation into the actual marine terminal at ordinary component scale. A coastal association alone is not full terminal correspondence.
